headline: Tuesday night's rain trended weaker and earlier overnight: every model now has only light rain, wettest about 7 to 10 PM Tuesday on a low, rising tide, far below street-flooding amounts.

summary.text: RRFS, yesterday's wettest model, fell from 0.30 to 0.08 in for its wettest 3 hours and ECMWF from 0.20 to 0.08 in. Consensus down from 0.14 to 0.11 in.
Wettest 3 hours, next 72 h: HRRR 0.15 (run ends 10 PM Tuesday, mid-rain), NBM 0.11, RRFS 0.08, ECMWF 0.08, GFS 0.08 in. HRRR is the wettest; no model has an hour above 0.06 in.
No street flooding expected on the consensus (0.11 in). Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour, roughly 6 times anything modeled.
Dry today and Tuesday daytime. Light rain starts 4 to 7 PM Tuesday; most models wettest 7 to 10 PM. NBM keeps light rain to about 4 AM Wednesday. Thanksgiving dry; weekend rain possible.
Rain falls near the -1.5 ft low at 6:28 PM Tuesday, so the channel can drain. Tides run about 1.4 ft above prediction at highs. Channel low and steady: 0.13 ft at Alameda.
Use today and Tuesday morning to clear street drain grates and yard drains. Tuesday's gusts may cause outages. Keep the page open Tuesday evening in case a downpour forms.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Dry today and tonight under a building ridge, with high clouds arriving. NWS San Francisco (3:26 AM) still calls Tuesday afternoon into Wednesday morning an impactful storm for rain and wind as a shortwave trough and cold front cross Northern California, but says NBM and some deterministic models have come down quite a bit on rain, and that a track farther north would lower amounts further. NWS rain totals: 0.4 to 1.0 in for the San Francisco Peninsula and 0.15 to 0.5 in for the East and South Bays; winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 40 mph near the coast and through gaps. Only a general thunder risk, best north of the Golden Gate. High pressure brings dry weather Thanksgiving and Friday; wet weather is favored for the weekend. NWS still expects major to extreme coastal flooding at the high tides through Thursday.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since last evening's discussion the models agree better, but on less rain and an earlier peak. Wettest 3 hours / total, 4 AM Monday to 4 AM Thursday:
• HRRR (2 AM Mon run, ends 10 PM Tuesday): 0.15 / 0.15 in, 7 to 10 PM Tuesday, 0.04 to 0.06 in per hour. Its first look at the storm, and it is cut off while still raining; the 15-minute output shows steady 0.012 to 0.016 in per 15 minutes from 7 PM to its end.
• NBM: 0.11 / 0.42 in, down from 0.14 / 0.52 in. Steady 0.03 to 0.04 in per hour from 4 PM Tuesday to 4 AM Wednesday, wettest 10 PM to 1 AM.
• RRFS (10 PM Sun run): 0.08 / 0.16 in, down from 0.30 / 0.46 in. The overnight burst near 1 AM is gone; light rain 7 to 10 PM Tuesday and one 0.06 in hour around 6 to 7 AM Wednesday.
• ECMWF: 0.08 / 0.13 in, down from 0.20 / 0.30 in, and moved from dawn Wednesday to 7 to 10 PM Tuesday.
• GFS: 0.08 / 0.10 in, nearly unchanged (0.10 in yesterday), also 7 to 10 PM Tuesday.

Consensus (HRRR 0.15 × 1.25 = 0.19, RRFS 0.08, NBM 0.11): middle value 0.11 in, down from 0.14 in. If anything this is a little low: HRRR ends mid-rain, and NWS's Peninsula range (0.4 to 1.0 in) is above every model's storm total here except NBM's. Even so, the largest modeled hour (0.06 in) is far from the 0.40 in one-hour burst level. The usual caveat: HRRR-type guidance has under-forecast local bursts by about 3×, and NWS keeps a slight thunder chance on the front.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model runs about 1.4 ft above the predicted high tides at Redwood City (1.0 to 1.7 ft at the lows). This morning's 9.2 ft high at 10:20 AM runs about 10.6 ft; tonight's 7.0 ft high at 12:16 AM Tuesday about 8.4 ft; Tuesday's 9.5 ft high at 11:02 AM about 10.9 ft. The timing now works in the street's favor: the predicted low is -1.5 ft at 6:28 PM Tuesday, and the model has the water near -0.3 ft at 7 PM, rising only to about 3.6 ft by 10 PM, so the main rain falls while the channel can drain freely. The model ends at 1 AM Wednesday at about 8.3 ft, still rising toward the predicted 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM, when NBM's light rain is still falling. Wednesday's 9.5 ft king tide at 11:46 AM comes after all models have the rain essentially over.

NWS: Coastal Flood Warning for the San Francisco Bay shoreline until 4 PM Thursday (the advisory expired at 6 AM). San Francisco high tides 2.2 ft above normal today, 2.6 ft Tuesday, 2.8 ft Wednesday and 2.4 ft Thursday, including up to 1.6 ft of surge, approaching the highest tide ever recorded there.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas it reads 0.13 ft at 4 AM, flat between 0.12 and 0.17 ft for 24 hours (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft). The gauge upstream of Caltrain last reported 0.07 ft at 5:13 PM Sunday (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft), about 11 hours ago.

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry and calm on the street early this morning. The Caltrain rain gauge recorded no rain in the 24 hours to its last report at 5:13 PM Sunday. NWS reports mainly clear skies with high clouds moving in and patchy fog in a few spots.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low through Tuesday afternoon: dry. Moderate for Tuesday evening into Wednesday morning: all five models now bring light rain, in a tight range (wettest 3 hours 0.08 to 0.15 in), and four of them peak 7 to 10 PM Tuesday. The open questions are how much rain HRRR shows after 10 PM once its later runs reach further, whether NWS's higher Peninsula totals or the lower point model totals verify, and whether a thunderstorm cell on the front gives a short downpour no model shows.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Nothing needed today beyond prep: clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains, and check sandbags.
• Tuesday afternoon and evening: winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 40 mph possible near the coast and through gaps; gusts can cause power outages, which slow the pumps.
• Tuesday evening: keep this page open; if a downpour develops, timestamped photos at the peak help.
• Stay away from the Bay shore and tidal sloughs at the late-morning high tides through Thursday; don't walk or drive through moving water.
